name: payjoin
title: B. Private payment vs PayJoin
summary: A BIP78 PayJoin. Breaks the common-input heuristic between the two parties, but the receiver's HTTPS endpoint (BIP21 pj=) sees the payer's network location and time, the receiver learns the payer's input UTXOs, and the chain still learns identifiers, amount, and time.

assumptions.join_kinds: ROOT_IDENTITY | RELATIONSHIP_IDENTITY | PAIRWISE_KEY | NETWORK_IDENTIFIER | SOURCE_ENDPOINT | DEST_ENDPOINT | TRANSACTION_ID | OBLIGATION_ID | CONTEXT_ID | RELATIONSHIP_LINK | ASSET | DENOMINATION | AMOUNT | TIME | CONTENT | CONTENT_SIZE | NETWORK_LOCATION | SESSION_IDENTIFIER

provenance: Authors' model of BIP78 payjoin disclosure (S11.B), 2026-09-03.
omitted: Whether the receiver's endpoint is Tor-hosted.
Global passive observers (out of threat model, S0).
not_better_when: You settle on-chain anyway: with the on-chain path the chain evidence is unchanged; PayJoin then becomes one Molt adapter with an honest manifest rather than a competitor.
joins_remaining_notes: This vector uses the credit path; with the on-chain path everything the chain would have seen remains.
The intermediary learns both relationship identities; reducing this belongs to whichever credit protocol implements the step.
Counterparties know each other by construction (bounded trust, not a leak).
